core.title: Map artifact names to REST endpoints via the endpoint pattern
core.given: An artifact named `{domain}:{resource}[.{category}]` is exposed to external consumers over a REST API
core.when: its artifact-to-REST endpoint mapping is specified or changed
core.then: Map the artifact name to an endpoint following `/{domain}s/{id}/{resource}[/{category}]`, with category facets adding path segments.
prefer: Pluralize the domain segment of the path, using regular English-style pluralization.
Turn each category facet of the artifact name into one extra path segment.
Follow the source's shorter forms where they apply: `session:new` -> `POST /sessions` (collection form, no `{id}` or resource segment); `player:identity` -> `GET /players/{id}` (no resource segment).

Select the HTTP verb from the resource keyword (creation -> POST, read -> GET, mutation -> PUT, removal -> DELETE): POST new/created/registered/started; GET result/active/config/events/foundations; PUT updated/closed/completed; DELETE terminated/deleted.
avoid: Hand-crafting paths that drop the plural domain or the category segments, or otherwise diverge from the pattern beyond the source's two shorter forms.
Choosing a verb that contradicts the resource keyword, e.g. mapping a mutation keyword such as `closed` to POST (closed -> PUT, not POST).
core.why: A deterministic artifact-to-REST mapping lets external consumers address artifacts over HTTP, and choosing the verb from the resource keyword keeps the API surface consistent with the artifact's lifecycle semantics.
evidence: Every externally exposed artifact has an endpoint matching `/{domain}s/{id}/{resource}[/{category}]` (or one of the source's example forms), with category facets as path segments.
Each declared HTTP verb matches the resource keyword table (POST/GET/PUT/DELETE).

Source examples hold: `ux:foundations` -> GET /uxs/{id}/foundations; `ux:foundations.colors` -> GET /uxs/{id}/foundations/colors; `match:result` -> GET /matches/{id}/result; `session:new` -> POST /sessions; `player:identity` -> GET /players/{id}.
verification: Pattern check: every externally exposed artifact has an endpoint matching `/{domain}s/{id}/{resource}[/{category}]` or one of the source's two shorter forms, with each category facet as a path segment.

Verb check: each declared HTTP verb matches the resource-keyword table (creation -> POST: new, created, registered, started; read -> GET: result, active, config, events, foundations; mutation -> PUT: updated, closed, completed; removal -> DELETE: terminated, deleted).
The check holds the source example set (evidence[2]) as positive fixtures, plus the negative verb example: a mutation keyword such as `closed` mapped to POST (closed -> PUT, not POST).

Do not flag the two source shorter forms (`session:new` -> the collection endpoint without `{id}` or a resource segment; `player:identity` -> no resource segment); the source does not state whether every creation keyword targets the collection, so do not generalize beyond the examples.
Domain pluralization is regular English-style pluralization (e.g. `match` -> `matches`).
The change fact needs a diff-level observer that extracts artifact-name -> endpoint/verb pairs from any changed file (plan artifacts, acceptances, docs, contracts, code).
Compliance is reviewer/LLM-judged; no automated implementation is specified (the reference realization ships none).

values: artifact-to-REST endpoint mapping specified or changed

fires: An artifact-to-REST endpoint mapping is written for an externally read artifact (e.g. a result artifact of a domain).
An acceptance or contract asserts the HTTP method or path for an externally exposed artifact (e.g. a creation or closure artifact).
A category-facet artifact gets an externally consumed endpoint.
doesNotFire: An artifact that is only consumed internally and never exposed over HTTP.
Boundary handler internals change with no artifact-to-endpoint mapping being specified or changed.
Edits that touch no artifact names or endpoints.

neutralityNotes: This is a naming/API-surface convention and is stack-neutral in substance: REST, HTTP and the URL path pattern are the subject matter of the rule, not stack machinery — a stack with no REST boundary simply does not adopt it. The artifact-name grammar `{domain}:{resource}[.{category}]` stays in the core because the endpoint pattern is defined over its parts; it is convention data, not structure data, so profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty. 'wagon' (the stack's bounded product slice) in why was neutralized to 'artifacts'. Concrete worked examples in prefer/avoid are not repeated in the core (the Bun sidecar is the delivered reference example); the full fixture set is preserved in evidence[2] and verification, and the two source shorter forms are kept verbatim in prefer[2] because they are normative exceptions that the core may neither drop (stronger) nor generalize (forbidden by verifier_detail[3]). The verb-mapping half remains a second de-facto obligation carried in prefer[3]; the realization's splitSuggestion (planner.interface.api-verb-mapping), term ids, audit and trace are realization metadata. unless is empty in the source.
